       Pursuant to Public Regulation Commission Procedures, 1.2.2.36(B) NMAC, and the July

28, 2026 Order on Post-Hearing Briefing, Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy (“CCAE”) and

Prosperity Works submit Post-Hearing Brief. In this brief, joint parties discuss the recovery

allocation for the Energy Affordability Program within the framework of mitigation of rate

increase for the low-income population.


      I.      INTRODUCTION

      Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy and Prosperity Works request the Commission

approve Comprehensive Stipulated Agreement (“Stipulation”). The Commission’s approval of

the Stipulation will further the public interest, in particular in implementing the Electric

Affordability Program (“EAP”) designed to suppress the financial impacts of excessive electric

utility rates on low-income populations. As explained by expert witness Alex Eubanks, the

Stipulation addresses concerns CCAE and Prosperity Works raised regarding Southwestern

Public Service Company’s (“SPS”) proposed EAP while providing an appropriate framework for

continued evaluation and improvement of the program. In sum, the Stipulation advances the

public interest through implementation of New Mexico's newly authorized low-income rates

while ensuring additional oversight, transparency, and stakeholder participation before future

modifications are considered.


      II.     LEGAL STANDARDS

       Stipulations, per 1.2.2.20 NMAC, are binding once approved by the Commission. This

confers a requirement that the Commission take a more active stance regarding stipulations and




                                                2
 the important regulatory schemes to be adhered to. 1 Hence, under the rules of procedure, the

Commission or presiding officer shall conduct a public hearing to determine whether a stipulation,

including the one before it, should be approved.2

        Parties to a stipulation must show that the stipulation is fair, just, reasonable and in the

public interest.3 They carry the burden to provide sufficient evidence and legal argument in order

for the Commission to approve it. 4 Sufficient evidence is a preponderance of the evidence as a

whole to support a conclusion that the stipulation is in the public interest. 5 Stipulations are

evaluated through asking three questions: (1) is the stipulation a product of serious bargaining

among capable, knowledgeable parties; (2) does the stipulation benefit ratepayers and the public

interest; and, (3) does the stipulation violate any regulatory principles or practices?6

        Under Section 62-8-6 1978 NMSA, no public utility shall as to rates or services grant any

unreasonable preference or advantage to any corporation or person within an classification. At

the same time, the Commission is not prohibited to approve rates and programs designed to reduce

the burden of energy costs on low-income customers.7 The Energy Affordability program

incorporated in the Stipulation may be approved pursuant to § 62-8-6(C).

       III.    ARGUMENT


              A. The Energy Affordability Program and Recovery Are the Result of
                 Serious Bargaining and they are in the Public Interest.

       The Energy Affordability Program proposed by SPS and eventually agreed to in the

Stipulation is a matter of first impression since § 62-8-6(C) became law. Parties to the Stipulation

all agreed under Section 1.12 that:

               (a) SPS shall update its affordability and budget analysis and
               evaluate whether the $750,000 annual budget is sufficient under
               current proposed rates. SPS shall provide the analysis in its next
               base rate case.

               (b) SPS shall make a one-time shareholder contribution of
               $750,000 to improve program reach, supplement benefits, or
               support outreach and administration.

               (c) SPS shall convene an EAP collaborative working group within
               60 days after approval of this Stipulation to evaluate
               implementation, data, reporting, eligibility, budget sufficiency,
               cost recovery, and future modifications. Recommendations
               from the working group will be included in SPS’s next base rate
               case.

               (d) SPS shall coordinate EAP implementation with other low-
               income programs, including energy efficiency, weatherization,
               LIHEAP, and customer outreach resources.


Significantly, the budget includes both the $750,000 annual budget proposed by SPS and a

shareholder contribution of $750,000. $750,000 in additional one-time shareholder resources can

expand the impact of the program. Other important considerations shared by the parties was the

need to conduct a budget analysis and to develop a workgroup to evaluate implementation, data,

reporting, eligibility, budget sufficiency, cost recovery, and future modifications.

       Cost recovery for the EAP is reasonable, even though it is spread across different classes

of ratepayers and a percentage of the EAP is funded by shareholders. As DOJ expert witness


                                                 4
 Doug Gegax explained, “I think that the fact that SPS does not put the burden solely on the

Residential Class to pay for this support, that other customer classes are also contributing is kind

of in line with my idea that everyone benefits, and therefore everyone should pay.”8 Issues of

inter- and intraclass recovery may be treated in the proposed EAP working group, as will related

issues of volumetric recovery versus a fixed charge. For this first EAP, however, the recovery

method agreed to is that costs for the program will be collected through a rider, and that method

may be evaluated by the future work group. If a different recovery method gets proposed in the

future, it could be included in the next rate case. Resolving these issues through an agreed-upon

settlement in this manner allows for the speedy initial implementation of a brand new, New

Mexico statute, while leaving room for future improvements to the program.

           The EAP is a reasonable program to include in the approval of this Stipulation. The

expanded budget allows SPS to enroll more low-income customers than the initial proposed

program, if SPS chooses to use the funding that way. The additional shareholder funding can

improve program reach, supplement benefits, or support outreach and administration. The EAP’s

efficacy and reach will continue to be evaluated through the working group, and recovery

mechanisms also be examined as a part of the next EAP that gets proposed.

           Finally, approval of the Stipulation with the inclusion of the new, agreed-to low income

EAP is in the public interest particularly because it mitigates rate increases for the most vulnerable

low-income utility customers.

        IV.     CONCLUSION

        The Stipulation is the result of serious bargaining that occurred among knowledgeable

parties. The inclusion of the EAP, while $1.5 million, is an effort to reduce the energy burden in

SPS territory, and is in the public interest.
